content: The combination of ipratropium and albuterol is prescribed to prevent symptoms such as wheezing, difficulty breathing, chest tightness, and coughing in individuals with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). COPD includes conditions like chronic bronchitis, which involves inflammation of the airways leading to the lungs, and emphysema, which is characterized by damage to the air sacs in the lungs. This combination medication is typically used when symptoms are not adequately controlled by a single inhaled medication. Both ipratropium and albuterol belong to a class of drugs known as bronchodilators. They work by relaxing and opening the airways in the lungs, making it easier to breathe. This medication is available as a liquid solution for inhalation via a nebulizer, which converts the medication into a mist, and as an aerosol for inhalation using an inhaler. It is generally used four times daily. It is crucial to follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the medication exactly as prescribed, without increasing or decreasing the dose or frequency unless directed by your doctor. If you experience symptoms such as wheezing, difficulty breathing, or chest tightness, your doctor may advise you to take additional doses. However, do not exceed two extra doses of the nebulizer solution or more than 12 puffs of the inhalation aerosol within 24 hours. If your symptoms worsen or the medication becomes less effective, contact your doctor immediately. If you find yourself needing the medication more frequently than usual, inform your doctor. For those using the inhaler, the medication is provided in canisters, each designed to deliver 200 inhalations. After using the labeled number of inhalations, the canister may no longer provide the correct dose, even if it still releases a spray. Keep track of the number of inhalations used and discard the canister once the labeled number is reached. Do not test the canister by floating it in water. Avoid getting the medication in your eyes, as it may cause or worsen narrow-angle glaucoma, a serious eye condition that can lead to vision loss. Symptoms of this condition include dilated pupils, eye pain or redness, blurred vision, and seeing halos around lights. If you accidentally get the medication in your eyes or develop these symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Always use the inhaler provided with the ipratropium and albuterol aerosol and do not use it with other medications. Similarly, do not use other inhalers with this medication. Avoid using the inhaler near open flames or heat sources, as it may explode if exposed to high temperatures. Before using the inhaler or nebulizer for the first time, read the accompanying instructions carefully. Ask your doctor, pharmacist, or respiratory therapist to demonstrate proper usage and practice under their supervision. Remove the protective dust cap and check the mouthpiece for debris. If the inhaler is being used for the first time or has not been used in over 24 hours, prime it by shaking it for at least 10 seconds and releasing three sprays into the air, away from your face. To use the inhaler, shake it well, exhale deeply, place the mouthpiece in your mouth, close your lips around it, and close your eyes. Inhale slowly and deeply while pressing down on the canister to release the medication. Hold your breath for 10 seconds, then remove the inhaler and exhale slowly. If a second puff is required, wait two minutes before repeating the process. Replace the protective cap after use. For the nebulizer, remove a vial of medication from the foil pouch and return the remaining vials to the pouch. Twist off the vial's top and empty the liquid into the nebulizer reservoir. Attach the reservoir to the mouthpiece or face mask and connect it to the compressor. Sit upright, place the mouthpiece in your mouth or wear the face mask, and turn on the compressor. Breathe deeply and evenly through your mouth for 5–15 minutes until the mist stops forming. Clean your inhaler or nebulizer regularly according to the manufacturer's instructions. This medication may be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before using ipratropium and albuterol, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to any of its components, including soya lecithin, soybeans, or peanuts. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, and supplements you are taking, as certain drugs may interact with this medication. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental procedures, let your healthcare provider know you are using this medication. Be aware that this medication may occasionally cause wheezing or difficulty breathing immediately after use; if this occurs, contact your doctor immediately and do not use the medication again unless instructed. Continue your normal diet unless otherwise directed by your doctor. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember, but skip it if it is almost time for your next dose. Do not double the dose to compensate for a missed one. Common side effects include cough, headache, nausea, heartburn, diarrhea, constipation, leg cramps, pain, difficulty urinating, frequent urination, pain during urination, and voice changes. Severe side effects requiring immediate medical attention include rapid heartbeat, chest pain, hives, rash, itching, swelling of the face or extremities, difficulty breathing or swallowing, and signs of infection such as fever or sore throat. Report any unusual symptoms to your doctor. Store this medication in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep unused vials in the foil pouch until ready for use. Store at room temperature, away from heat and moisture. Do not puncture or incinerate the aerosol canister. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, consulting your pharmacist if needed. In case of overdose, contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222 or call 911 if the individual collapses or stops breathing. Symptoms of overdose may include chest pain and rapid heartbeat. Keep all medical appointments and do not share this medication with others. Consult your pharmacist for any questions about refills. This medication is sold under the brand names Combivent® and Duoneb®.
